newsitem.title: UK: UK Soco to start Mongolia oil sales to China in July.
newsitem.headline: UK Soco to start Mongolia oil sales to China in July.

text.p: British-based oil explorer Soco International on Tuesday said it planned to start deliveries of crude into China from its Sotoma oil find in Mongolia in July.

Soco Chief Financial Officer Roger Cagle said a fourth discovery well, announced on Monday, had confirmed the commercial potential of the field which lies near Mongolia's Chinese border in a 40,000 square kilometre frontier concession.
"What we have here is a confirmation of Mongolia's potential for the market," said Cagle.
Soco was listed at the end of May on the London stock exchange.
The company, now running test production from Sotamo, is importing production facilities and plans to build a 300 kilometer pipeline to China starting in 1999.
Truck exports of 500 barrels a day (bpd) of the 37 degree API crude are expected to rise to some 20,000 bpd when the pipeline is in place, Cagle said.
The crude will be priced at China's Daqing blend less a $2 a barrel transportation cost.
Soco has hit oil in four of six wells drilled in its Mongolia concession so far.
It plans drilling two more wells this year, eight in 1998 and 17 in 1999.
Soco shares were up 20.5 pence at 257 pence on Tuesday morning, just 3 pence below their placing price when the company was floated to raise money for its Mongolia operations on May 31.
